title: No post-run failure triage: no success/fail summary, no failed-only view, no re-run-failed-hosts
existing_state: After a multi-host run, the status bar reports only a flat count — "Completed execution on {resultCount} hosts" (Form1.cs:12676, 12774) — with no success/failure breakdown; folder runs do slightly better with a status-bar "{successCount} succeeded, {failCount} failed" (Form1.cs:12958-12964) but never say WHICH hosts failed. Per-host outcomes ARE captured: ExecutionResult.Success/WasCancelled are rolled into HostExecutionContext (Form1.cs:13115, 13141) and HostHistoryEntry (Models/AppConfiguration.cs:428-437, Form1.cs:13255-13256), and the history host pane owner-draws a green check / red X / amber square per host (Form1.cs:8541-8583). But that is the end of the road: the history context menus offer only Save/Delete/View Details/Export Host Output (Form1.cs:8358-8399, 8814-8840), the host list has no failed-only filter or failure count, grid rows are never marked with execution results (only connection tests paint cells — SetConnectionTestVisualState at Form1.cs:8926), and there is no retry mechanism anywhere (a repo-wide search for rerun/retry-failed finds only script-level send.retry and update-download retry). A user who runs a preset against 200 devices and gets 18 failures must visually scan the host list for red X icons, note the IPs by hand, find and check those rows in the grid, and run again.
recommendation: All the data already exists in memory at run completion (the results list in ExecutePresetOnRowsAsync, Form1.cs:12400-12437 and 12463-12496). (1) Change completionStatus to include the breakdown, e.g. "Completed: 182 succeeded, 18 failed" with a red tint when failures > 0. (2) Paint per-row result indicators in the host grid after any multi-host run by reusing the connection-test visual-state mechanism (SetConnectionTestVisualState / ApplyConnectionTestCellResult, Form1.cs:8920-8937). (3) Add a "Show failed only" toggle above lstHosts that filters the host pane to !Success entries. (4) Add "Check failed hosts in grid" and "Re-run on failed hosts" actions (post-run button plus history host-pane context-menu items, disabled when the entry has zero failures): match HostHistoryEntry.HostAddress back to grid rows by IP:port (reuse HostConnection.Parse + TryGetExplicitPortFromHostValue at Form1.cs:13401, same as UpdateHostColumn at Form1.cs:14190), check those rows and uncheck the rest, then invoke the existing ExecuteOnCheckedHosts() (Form1.cs:12753) — the Ansible '--limit @retry' equivalent.
user_benefit: Turns the most common fleet-ops loop (run, find failures, retry failures) from minutes of error-prone scan-and-transcribe across 200 rows into two clicks. Table stakes in Ansible (retry files) and comparable tools.

title: Scheduled job outcomes never reach the notification system or output panel — nightly failures are silent
existing_state: The app has a complete multi-channel NotificationService (SMTP, Teams, Toast, Webhook, with profiles, mentions, attachments; SendAsync at Services/Notifications/NotificationService.cs:83-114), but scheduled-job outcomes never use it. JobExecutionService.NotificationService (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:75) is only threaded into the per-run SshExecutionService (JobExecutionService.cs:410) to power the YAML `notify` script command — NotifyCommand.cs:66 is the sole caller of SendAsync — so a job only notifies if its script author hand-wrote notify steps, and a job that fails before/outside the script (credential resolution, connection failure, missing preset) can never notify. Form1's handlers do nothing user-visible: OnSchedulerJobCompleted (Form1.cs:15250-15256) just removes the id from _runNowJobIds and refreshes the status-bar countdown; OnSchedulerJobStateChanged (Form1.cs:15299-15304) only refreshes the status bar — despite the wiring comment 'Subscribe to execution events for output panel notifications' (Form1.cs:15073). A complete, tested formatter exists for exactly this — SchedulerNotificationFormatter.FormatCompletion/FormatStateChange (Utilities/SchedulerNotificationFormatter.cs:16-64) with [Scheduled:]/[Run Now:]/[Skipped:] prefixes — yet production code only calls ShouldShowStatusBar/FormatStatusBar/FormatTimeRemaining; FormatCompletion/FormatStateChange are referenced solely by tests, and the _runNowJobIds set (Form1.cs:167, 15309) exists only to pick a prefix that is never rendered. JobDefinition has zero notification-related fields. Net effect: a 2 AM backup job fails and there is no toast, no email, no Teams message, not even an output-panel line; the user finds out only by opening the Job List dialog and checking the Last Result column.
recommendation: Two layers, both cheap given the existing pieces: (1) In Form1.OnSchedulerJobCompleted/OnSchedulerJobStateChanged, render SchedulerNotificationFormatter.FormatCompletion/FormatStateChange (using _runNowJobIds for the prefix — what it was built for) into the main output panel, red on failure. (2) Add per-job notification policy to JobDefinition (NotifyOnFailure defaulting from a global 'Notify on scheduled job failure' setting, NotifyOnSuccess opt-in, optional NotificationProfileName) surfaced as a small group on the JobEditorDialog Advanced tab; on JobCompleted per policy, dispatch via NotificationService.SendAsync (either inside JobExecutionService before raising the event, or in a small subscriber alongside JobHistoryService which already subscribes at Services/JobHistoryService.cs:41) with job name, host success/fail counts, ErrorMessage, and duration; failure-only by default to avoid noise from frequent cron jobs. A config-level default gives existing jobs failure alerts without re-editing each one.
user_benefit: The entire point of a scheduler is unattended operation; today a failed nightly device backup against 200 hosts is invisible until someone manually opens the Job List dialog. This turns the existing notification machinery into actual ops alerting — table stakes for any scheduler (cron + mail, Ansible Tower, Rundeck).

title: Host grid has no filter/search — only way to find a host among hundreds is scrolling
existing_state: The host grid (dgv_variables) has no search or filter capability of any kind. The app's only Find feature (Ctrl+F) is hard-wired to the output pane: Form1.cs:14490-14492 anchors FindDialog to txtOutput and Form1.cs:14516 navigates matches via txtOutput.SelectionStart. Meanwhile the preset tree DOES have a debounced search box with 'Filter presets...' placeholder (Form1.cs:8967-8982, predicates at 9080-9099), so the app already has the pattern — it just was never applied to hosts. With 200 devices, locating one host or checking a subset (e.g. all rows whose 'site' column is 'DC2') means manual scrolling and clicking checkboxes one by one; the bulk-selection affordances are limited to Select All / Deselect All / Invert (Form1.cs:6523-6546).
recommendation: Add a filter bar above the host grid mirroring the existing preset search panel: a text box (with optional column-scope dropdown defaulting to 'All columns'), live row hiding via DataGridViewRow.Visible, a match counter, and a 'Check matching' / 'Uncheck matching' action so a filter can drive run-target selection. Reuse the InitializePresetSearchFilter debounce-timer pattern (Form1.cs:8967+). Two integration points need care: the hand-rolled scrollbar math must recompute on visibility changes (UpdateDataGridViewScrollbars, Form1.cs:890-966), and SetAllCheckboxes/select-all should operate on visible rows while a filter is active.
user_benefit: For a fleet operator this is the single biggest daily friction: 'run this on all branch routers' becomes type-filter + Check matching instead of scrolling 200 rows ticking boxes. Also brings the grid up to parity with the app's own preset tree.

title: No find, replace, or go-to-line in the script editor — Ctrl+F always targets the output pane
existing_state: Form1.ProcessCmdKey routes Ctrl+F unconditionally to ShowFindDialog (Form1.cs:14462-14464) regardless of whether the script editor has focus, and that dialog is hardwired to the output box: the seed comes from txtOutput.SelectedText (Form1.cs:14484), it anchors to txtOutput (Form1.cs:14492), and BuildMatchList scans txtOutput.Text only (Form1.cs:14583-14599). F3/Shift+F3 likewise navigate output matches only (Form1.cs:14472-14477). FindDialog itself is search-only — a find textbox, prev/next, match-case/whole-word/regex toggles, no replace field, and it takes Form1 directly in its constructor (FindDialog.cs:21-38). There is no editor search anywhere: grep finds no SearchInTarget/Scintilla find usage in Services/Editor or elsewhere. Result: while editing a multi-hundred-line YAML preset there is zero way to search the script, replace a variable name used 30 times, or jump to the line number a validation error cites — the user scrolls manually or round-trips through an external editor. The same gap applies to the second editor host in JobEditorDialog. Meanwhile RunOutputViewerDialog already ships its own local Ctrl+F search bar (RunOutputViewerDialog.cs:200-204, 328-365), so the app has set the expectation that Ctrl+F is context-local.
recommendation: Add an in-editor find/replace to ScintillaScriptEditorControl itself (so both Form1's txtCommand and JobEditorDialog's custom-preset editor get it for free): handle Ctrl+F/Ctrl+H/Ctrl+G in the control, show a small overlay strip in the editor's top-right (copy the existing FindDialog visual language), and implement search via Scintilla's TargetStart/TargetEnd/SearchInTarget plus an indicator to highlight all matches (indicator indexes 8/9 are taken by squiggles; use a free one). Replace uses ReplaceTarget wrapped in one undo action like AcceptCurrentCompletion does (UI/ScintillaScriptEditorControl.cs:1344-1357). In Form1.ProcessCmdKey, route Ctrl+F to the editor when txtCommand.Focused, else keep the existing output find; F3/Shift+F3 should follow whichever target was last searched (extracting the Form1-specific callbacks into a small IFindTarget interface keeps both paths sharing one implementation).
user_benefit: Editing real-world presets (200-device runbooks easily exceed 300 lines) becomes practical inside the app: rename a variable, find every 'send:' touching an interface, jump to the line an error message names — and Ctrl+F stops doing the wrong thing when the editor is focused. This is the single largest gap versus VS Code/SecureCRT-class editors.

title: Interactive terminal has no UI entry point — opening a shell on a host requires authoring a YAML interactive: step
existing_state: A complete professional terminal stack exists (Rebex VirtualTerminal emulation, owner-drawn viewport with scrollback/selection/auto-copy, dark theming), but the ONLY way to reach it is authoring a YAML preset containing an `interactive:` step, dispatched through InteractiveCommand.ExecuteAsync (Services/Scripting/Commands/InteractiveCommand.cs:13-28) into InteractiveTerminalService.RunAsync (Services/Terminal/InteractiveTerminalService.cs:231). InteractiveTerminalForm is only ever constructed inside the service (InteractiveTerminalService.cs:824, 1777), and grep confirms no other code path instantiates it. There is no menu item, toolbar button, or host-grid context-menu entry anywhere — the string 'Terminal' does not appear once in Form1.Designer.cs, the host grid's right-click menu offers only "Test Connection(s)" / "Clear Test Results" plus column/row/selection ops (Form1.cs:8848-8861, Form1.Designer.cs:343-402), and the feature is documented only in the GitHub-hosted SCRIPTING.md (line 2648). RunSeparateAsync (InteractiveTerminalService.cs:335-357) already dials a fresh standalone SSH session from host + resolved credentials, so the plumbing for ad-hoc sessions exists. A user who just ran a fleet command and wants to poke at one failing device must leave the app for PuTTY/SecureCRT.
recommendation: Add "Open Terminal" to the host-grid context menu (next to "Test Connection(s)" in Form1.cs InitializeConnectionTesting, ~line 8848) and optionally as a double-click action on the selected host row. Cheapest robust implementation: synthesize a one-step script (`- interactive: {session: separate}`) for the selected host and run it through the existing single-host execution path — this reuses credential resolution (including per-host username/password/vault_path columns), timeouts, the session audit trail, and the history "Interactive" tab for free. Alternatively extract RunSeparateAsync's context dependencies (CurrentHost, ResolvedUsername/Password, Timeouts) into a small parameter object so the launcher can call the service directly without a ScriptContext. Per Development Guideline 1, keep the launch logic in the service; Form1 only wires the menu item.
user_benefit: Eliminates the constant app-switch to PuTTY/SecureCRT: after a fleet run flags one device, the operator can drop into a live shell on it in one click — table stakes for any SSH management tool, and it finally makes the already-built terminal emulator discoverable.

title: No global exception handler, no application log file, no crash reporting — Release-build diagnostics evaporate
existing_state: Program.cs:59 runs `Application.Run(new Form1())` with no try/catch, and a repo-wide search finds zero registrations of Application.ThreadException, AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException, TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException, or SetUnhandledExceptionMode. There is no logging framework anywhere (no ILogger/Serilog/NLog/Trace/EventLog and no log file under %LocalAppData%\SSH_Helper). The only diagnostic channel is Debug.WriteLine (35 occurrences across 9 files), which compiles to a no-op in Release. Concrete diagnostics that vanish for end users: the scheduler's entire evaluation loop failure is caught and Debug.WriteLine-only (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:325-327) — if it throws repeatedly, scheduled jobs silently stop firing with zero trace; losing the scheduler lock to another instance logs only Debug.WriteLine (Form1.cs:15103); an InheritFromApp job with a username but missing app-level password logs the real cause only to Debug.WriteLine (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:620) then passes the throw-guard at :388-393 (which requires BOTH username and password empty) and runs with an empty password, so job history records generic per-host auth failures instead of 'password missing'. User-facing error dialogs show only ex.Message with the stack discarded (e.g. Form1.cs:12442, 12501, 12969). An unhandled exception in the 15k-line Form1 produces the stock .NET crash dialog with no state flush and nothing the user can send the developer.
recommendation: In Program.Main register Application.ThreadException + AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException + TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException handlers that append exception, app version (Form1.ApplicationVersion), and timestamp to a rolling log under AppDataPaths.GetAppFolder()/logs/, then show a themed crash dialog with 'Copy details' and 'Open log folder' actions. Add a tiny static FileLog helper (one class in Utilities/) and route the existing Debug.WriteLine sites — at minimum JobExecutionService.cs:327/620/1019 and Form1.cs:15103 — through it so scheduler failures are diagnosable in Release. Error dialogs can then append 'Details were written to the log.'
user_benefit: Today a crash or a silently-dead scheduler is undebuggable — there is literally nothing on disk to look at. A log file plus a crash handler turns 'it just stopped working' support cases into one-file diagnoses.

title: No jump-host/bastion (ProxyJump) support for reaching devices behind a management host
existing_state: There is no proxy or jump-host capability anywhere in the SSH layer: a repo-wide grep for ProxyJump/ProxyCommand/proxy/jump/bastion finds no SSH-related hits. The OpenSSH config parser explicitly supports only six directives — HostName, Port, User, IdentityFile, HostKeyAlgorithms, Ciphers (Utilities/SshConfigParser.cs:8, 12-15) — so ProxyJump lines in a user's existing ~/.ssh/config are silently ignored, and both connect paths (SshExecutionService.CreateConnectedClientWithFallback at 2365+ and SshConnectionPool.CreateConnectionAsync) dial the target IP directly. Network fleets very commonly sit behind a bastion/management host; users of OpenSSH, SecureCRT (firewall sessions), and Ansible all get this natively, and such users simply cannot reach their devices with this app today.
recommendation: Add jump-host support: parse ProxyJump in SshConfigParser (plus an optional per-environment/global 'Jump host' setting with its own credentials), then implement connection-via-bastion in both connect paths — Rebex supports this via an Ssh session to the bastion plus local port forwarding (or its Settings.Proxy SOCKS support pointed at a bastion-side tunnel). Pool the bastion connection itself so 20 parallel target connections share one bastion session. Scope v1 to a single hop.
user_benefit: Unlocks the app for the very common topology where 200 devices are only reachable through a management bastion — currently a hard blocker that forces those users back to scripts over plain OpenSSH.

evidence.note: SupportedOptions set contains only six directives; ProxyJump silently dropped
Direct client.Connect(host.IpAddress, host.Port) — no tunnel/proxy hook
Pool connect path equally direct; bastion session pooling would slot in here

title: IPv6 hosts cannot be used anywhere — literals are mangled at parse, rejected by validation, and silently skipped in multi-host runs
existing_state: HostConnection.Parse splits the host string on ':' (Models/HostConnection.cs:45-51), so an IPv6 literal like 2001:db8::1 becomes IpAddress "2001" with the rest discarded; there is no bracket syntax ([addr]:port) handling, and ToString() (HostConnection.cs:92) would emit an ambiguous addr:port for IPv6. Validation is equally closed: InputValidator.IsValidHostOrIp uses LastIndexOf(':') and then accepts only UriHostNameType.IPv4 or Dns, with an in-code comment 'no IPv6 support here' (Utilities/InputValidator.cs:49-82); HostConnection.IsValid (HostConnection.cs:59-65) routes to the same validator. This validator gates every execution entry point: single-host runs refuse with 'No valid host selected' (Form1.cs:12738, 12805), Flow Canvas test-step refuses (Form1.cs:7110), and — worst — the multi-host connection builder silently `continue`s past the row (Form1.cs:13314), so in a 200-device run an IPv6 row simply produces no result and no error. For a fleet SSH tool aimed at network operators this is a missing capability as dual-stack and v6-only management networks become common — entries are silently mis-parsed rather than rejected with a message.
recommendation: Add bracket-aware parsing: in HostConnection.Parse, treat '[...]' as the host (with optional ':port' suffix) and treat a bare string containing 2+ colons as a portless IPv6 literal (Uri.CheckHostName already classifies these as IPv6); update IsValidHostOrIp to accept UriHostNameType.IPv6 for both forms; make ToString() emit [addr]:port when Port != 22. Verify pass-through at the two client layers (Rebex session setup and SSH.NET) and the connection-pool key — both libraries accept IPv6 strings natively, so the work concentrates in the model/utility files plus grid validation messages. Independently of IPv6, change the silent skip at Form1.cs:13314 to emit a per-row 'skipped: invalid host' line into the run output so rows can never vanish from a fleet run unannounced.
user_benefit: Unblocks IPv6/dual-stack environments entirely (increasingly the default in service-provider and modern enterprise gear), and guarantees that no host row can silently disappear from a 200-host run.

evidence.note: Split(':') parsing mangles IPv6 literals; IsValid delegates to IsValidHostOrIp; ToString emits ambiguous IPv6:port

title: No retry/backoff for failed scheduled jobs — one transient blip means the run is missed until the next cron occurrence
existing_state: There is no retry concept anywhere in the scheduler. JobDefinition has no retry fields (grep for Retry/MaxAttempts/attempt in Models/JobDefinition.cs: no matches; the only 'attempt' mention in the 1119-line JobExecutionService is a comment at line 386), and the failure paths simply record the failure and stop: ExecuteScheduledJobAsync catches the exception, calls HandlePostExecution + OnJobFailed and completes (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:345-375); a partial host failure marks the run Failed (JobExecutionService.cs:433-435, 467-470) with no re-attempt of the failed hosts. The next attempt is whenever the cron fires again — for a nightly backup that is 24 hours later. One-time jobs are worse: a failed scheduled one-time run auto-disables the job permanently with reason "One-time schedule failed" (JobExecutionService.cs:875-889). The codebase already anticipates repeated failures — JobHistoryService.TryCollapseLatestFailure (Services/JobHistoryService.cs:237-312) collapses identical consecutive failures with ConsecutiveFailureCount. Every comparable scheduler (Windows Task Scheduler 'retry every X up to N times', Ansible Tower, cron wrappers) offers retry-on-failure.
recommendation: Add per-job retry policy to JobDefinition (e.g. MaxRetries 0-5 default 0, RetryDelayMinutes) with editor fields on the JobEditorDialog Advanced tab next to the existing timeout overrides. In HandlePostExecution / ExecuteJobCoreAsync, when a scheduled (non-cancelled, non-RunNow) run fails and attempts remain, schedule a delayed re-dispatch — e.g. track NextRetryUtc per job and let the existing 30-second evaluation timer pick it up via IsJobDue — instead of waiting for the next cron occurrence. Record the attempt number in JobRunResult/JobRunRecord so history shows 'Failed (attempt 2/3)' then 'OK'; the existing failure-collapse logic keeps history compact. For one-time jobs, only mark 'One-time schedule failed' after retries are exhausted. Consider retrying only the failed hosts for partial failures, since results are already per-host.
user_benefit: Transient SSH/network failures at 2 AM are the norm in fleet operations; today each one costs a full day's backup for the affected job (or permanently kills a one-time job). Automatic retry closes the most common unattended-failure gap versus Task Scheduler/Ansible.

title: 31-script sample library never reaches users: not shipped in releases, no in-app browser; default presets are two unlabeled FortiGate one-liners
existing_state: ScriptSamples/ holds 31+ curated YAML scripts across bash/, cisco/, checkpoint/, fortigate/, generic/, libraries/, qa/ plus a 215-line tutorial README — and every sample is CI-validated (parsed and strictly validated by CanonicalCommandMapSyntaxTests.cs:218-243), so they are guaranteed-working documentation. But release artifacts contain only the two exes, checksums, README.md and SCRIPTING.md (.github/workflows/build-release.yml:126-135) — samples are neither zipped nor embedded — and nothing references them from the application: the string 'ScriptSamples' appears only in test code, SSH_Helper.csproj has no Content/None item for the folder (only rebex.key is copied, :54), and ScriptSamples/README.md:202-206 literally instructs 'Copy the script content into a preset' — impossible for anyone running an installed build. Meanwhile a first-run user's entire preset tree is CreateDefaultConfiguration's two hardcoded presets (Services/ConfigurationService.cs:427-440): 'Custom' = 'get system status' and 'Get external-address-resource list' — both FortiGate CLI, unlabeled as samples and meaningless against Linux/Cisco targets. So the app's deepest feature (the 40+-command YAML engine) presents itself on day one as two vendor-specific one-liners. Note: FLOW_CANVAS_ENHANCEMENTS.md:220-222 proposes only a canvas-side 'First Light' empty state with an 'Open a sample' action — it does not cover preset-library-wide sample access or shipping samples at all.
recommendation: Embed ScriptSamples/**/*.yaml as assembly resources (copy the IncludeFlowCanvasDistEmbeddedResources pattern, SSH_Helper.csproj:100-110) and add a 'New preset from sample...' gallery dialog reachable from the preset-tree context menu (next to the existing ctxImportPreset, Form1.Designer.cs:678) and Help/File menus: left tree grouped by vendor folder, read-only syntax-highlighted preview with the sample's header-comment description and required CSV columns, and a 'Create preset in folder: [dropdown]' button that drops the YAML into a new preset via the existing preset-save path. Rename or replace the two FortiGate defaults to make their vendor explicit (e.g. folder 'Samples (FortiGate)') or seed defaults from the generic/ samples. As a zero-code stopgap, add a ScriptSamples.zip step to the release job. The same embedded catalog can later back the Flow Canvas 'Open a sample' roadmap item.
user_benefit: New users get working, runnable demonstrations of the scripting engine (loops, extract, webhook, JSON reporting) in two clicks instead of never discovering that YAML scripting exists; the 31 regression-tested scripts the project already maintains finally reach the people they were written for.

title: Job editor never shows what a Preset/Folder job will actually run, and offers no Run Now / test from the editor
existing_state: For jobs targeting a saved preset or folder, the Content tab is dead space: the Scintilla editor is only ever populated with the job's own CustomPresetCommands (JobEditorDialog.cs:1581) and for non-custom targets it just goes read-only with the hint 'Saved preset and folder jobs ignore this tab' (UpdateCustomPresetEditorState, JobEditorDialog.cs:661-668). A user authoring or reviewing a job sees only the preset's NAME in a combo (General tab) — to verify what commands will run at 3 AM against 200 devices they must close the editor, open the preset elsewhere, and come back. The dialog already resolves the target preset object for timeout guidance (GetInheritedCommandTimeoutInfo, JobEditorDialog.cs:1533-1550), so the content is at hand. There is also no way to trigger or dry-run the job from the editor (no Test/Run affordance anywhere in JobEditorDialog.cs); Run Now exists only back in the JobListDialog toolbar (JobListDialog.cs:1061-1076) after saving and re-selecting.
recommendation: Two additions to JobEditorDialog: (1) when target type is Preset or Folder, populate the Content tab's existing read-only Scintilla editor with the resolved preset content (for folders, concatenate per-preset with header comments) and change the help label to 'Read-only preview of target preset content as of now'; PresetManager.Get/GetPresetsInFolder are already injected. (2) Add a 'Save & Run Now' button next to Save that sets a flag the JobListDialog caller can act on after _jobStorage.Save (it already owns the _runNowInvoker delegate), so a new job can be smoke-tested in one step.
user_benefit: Eliminates the close-editor/open-preset/reopen-editor round trip when vetting what a scheduled job will execute, and lets a freshly authored job be tested immediately — the single most common 'did I wire this up right?' moment.

evidence.note: Content editor read-only + ignored for Preset/Folder targets; only ever loaded from job.CustomPresetCommands
Editor already resolves the target preset via _presetManager for timeout guidance — content is one call away
Save flow returns to JobListDialog which owns _runNowInvoker — natural seam for Save & Run Now

title: Execution history has no search, filter, or useful metadata — finding last week's failed run means scrolling labels
existing_state: The history surface is a plain ListBox of labels (lstOutput, Form1.cs:1006 sets DisplayMember to Label) whose context menu offers only Save As / Save All / Delete / Delete All / View Details (contextHistoryLst_Opening, Form1.cs:8358-8374). The on-disk index entry stores only Id, Label, CreatedAtUtc, two booleans, and a filename (Models/HistoryIndex.cs:15-23) — no preset name, no environment, no host count, no success/failure status — even though all of that exists in the ExecutionDetails payload being written at the same moment (Form1.cs:13009, 14240). There is no text search across run outputs, no date or status filter, and no way to answer "which run touched host 10.1.2.3" without opening entries one by one.
recommendation: Enrich HistoryIndexEntry with PresetName, EnvironmentName, HostCount, FailedHostCount (populate in the two SaveRun call sites; old entries just render without badges — SchemaVersion already exists for migration). Add a filter textbox above lstOutput that narrows by label/preset/environment, plus a status filter (all / had failures). For content search, add a "Search outputs..." action that streams run files with the existing selective deserializer (HistoryStorageService already has lightweight readers) and lists matching runs.
user_benefit: For someone running daily jobs against 200 devices, history is the audit trail. Ansible/SecureCRT users expect to query past runs; today the only navigation is scrolling a label list capped at MaxHistoryEntries.

evidence.note: context menu = save/delete/details only; no search or filter affordance
index entry carries no queryable metadata beyond label and timestamp
SaveRun call site where ExecutionDetails (preset, environment, host results) is in hand

mockup_idea: History panel before/after: before = flat label list; after = search box on top, each row showing label + preset/environment chips + a red '3 failed' badge, with a status filter dropdown.

title: Steps cannot be named/labeled — output, history, and canvas show only command type + line number
existing_state: The event contract already reserves a slot for a user-defined step name (StepExecutionEventArgs.StepName, documented as "The step's user-defined name, if any" at ScriptExecutor.cs:27-28), but the executor hardcodes it to null in both StepStarting (ScriptExecutor.cs:374) and StepCompleted (ScriptExecutor.cs:402). ScriptStep has no name/label property at all (the only 'Name' hit in Models/ScriptStep.cs is a notification-profile comment at line 1321), and `name` is absent from the step-level KnownStepKeys list (ScriptParser.cs:24-69), so writing `name: Backup config` on a step today is rejected as a blocking unknown-key error (unknown keys produce did-you-mean errors). Every consumer — run output, history, and the Flow Canvas per-block panels — can only identify a step as e.g. "send (line 12)". Ansible (`- name: ...`), GitHub Actions, and every comparable runner treat per-task names as table stakes for reading multi-host run logs. FLOW_CANVAS_ENHANCEMENTS.md covers branch labels/frames but not user step names (checked lines 24, 95, 142, 283) — no roadmap overlap.
recommendation: Add `Name` (string?) to ScriptStep, add "name" to KnownStepKeys plus a step-root parse case next to `when`/`capture` (ScriptParser.cs:997-999), and pass `step.Name` into both event constructions at ScriptExecutor.cs:374/402. Then surface it: prefix run-output step lines and history step records with the name when present, and let FlowCanvasBridge carry it into the node payload so canvas blocks render the friendly name as their title (per Development Guideline 8 this needs the React side too). Snippet round-trip in the bridge preserves the key automatically since it rides the step's YAML verbatim.
user_benefit: On a 200-device run, output that reads "Backup running-config — OK (1.2s)" instead of "send (line 12)" makes failures locatable at a glance, and canvas blocks self-document the script.

evidence.note: StepName field documented as user-defined but always passed null
KnownStepKeys has no `name`; unknown step keys are blocking errors
no Name/label property anywhere on the step model

mockup_idea: Before/after of the run output pane and a canvas block: before shows "send (line 12) ✓ 1.2s" and a block titled "send"; after shows "Backup running-config ✓ 1.2s" and the block header reading "Backup running-config" with the command type as a small subtitle chip.

title: Terminal has no find-in-scrollback, and the only buffer actions hide in the invisible system menu
existing_state: There is no search capability anywhere in the terminal (grep for find/search across Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs and UI/InteractiveTerminalViewportControl.cs: zero hits) — to locate an error in 10,000 lines of device output the user must scroll manually or Copy All into another editor. The three buffer actions that do exist ("Copy All to Clipboard", "Clear Scrollback", "Reset Terminal") are appended to the Win32 system menu via AppendMenu P/Invoke (Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:545-558, dispatched in WndProc 235-258) — reachable only by clicking the window icon or Alt+Space, an affordance new users will never discover. There is also no "Save buffer to file": full transcripts land in history's Interactive tab after the fact, but nothing exports the live buffer (CopyAllToClipboard at form 488-507 is clipboard-only).
recommendation: Add a Ctrl+F find bar (small overlay docked top-right of the viewport) that searches the full Rebex buffer including history — the data access already exists via the same path BuildClipboardText uses (InteractiveTerminalService.cs Copy All provider) — with next/previous, highlight via the existing selection mechanism, and Esc to dismiss. Move/duplicate Copy All, Clear Scrollback, Reset Terminal, plus a new "Save Buffer As…", into a normal right-click context menu (relocating paste to a menu item alongside, which also makes paste discoverable) or a slim toolbar.
user_benefit: Finding one failed interface in a wall of 'show interface' output goes from copy-everything-into-Notepad to two keystrokes; the buffer actions users already paid for become discoverable.

evidence.note: Buffer actions only exist as system-menu (Alt+Space) entries via AppendMenu P/Invoke
CopyAllToClipboard is clipboard-only; no save-to-file
No find/search code exists in the viewport or form (verified by grep)

title: No structured (CSV/JSON) export of per-host results — only plain-text transcripts
existing_state: All result exports are flat text: SaveHistoryEntry writes the whole concatenated run transcript to one .txt (Form1.cs:14265-14285), SaveAllHistory concatenates every run into one .txt (Form1.cs:14296-14342), and the per-host export writes a single host's output to .txt (Form1.cs:8814-8840). Yet the per-host structured data already exists in every history payload — HostHistoryEntry has HostAddress, Success, WasCancelled, Timestamp, Label (Models/AppConfiguration.cs:428-437). There is no way to produce the artifact a fleet operator actually reports with: a host-by-host status table (which of the 300 hosts succeeded/failed and why) that can be opened in Excel or fed to another tool. Comparing output across hosts is also manual — multi-selecting hosts just concatenates outputs (BuildSelectedHostOutput, Form1.cs:8515), even though a diff engine already exists in the codebase (Utilities/InlineDiffBuilder.cs, currently used only by UnsavedPresetDiffDialog).
recommendation: Add "Export Results as CSV..." to the history list context menu: one row per HostHistoryEntry with host, status (OK/FAILED/CANCELLED), timestamp, label/error, optional truncated or full output column; reuse CsvManager's escaping. Consider a sibling JSON export for tooling. As a follow-on, add a two-host "Compare outputs" view reusing InlineDiffBuilder for drift triage across hosts.
user_benefit: Produces the report every fleet change actually ends with — a spreadsheet of per-host outcomes — in one click, instead of hand-parsing a concatenated text transcript.

evidence.note: single-entry and all-history exports are concatenated .txt only
structured per-host fields already persisted in payloads

title: parse command supports only FortiGate — no Cisco IOS or generic parser despite advertising multi-format
existing_state: ParserFactory registers exactly two format names, 'fortigate' and 'fortios', both mapping to the same FortiGateParser (Services/Scripting/Parsers/ParserFactory.cs:11-16). Any other format throws 'Unsupported configuration format' (:32-35). Yet ParseCommand's own doc comment claims it 'Supports FortiGate and other network device configuration formats' (Services/Scripting/Commands/ParseCommand.cs:10-11), and IConfigParser's doc even names 'cisco-ios' as an example format (Services/Scripting/Parsers/IConfigParser.cs:11) — the abstraction was built for multi-vendor but never filled in. A related authoring trap: parse's 'from' takes a bare variable name via GetVariableString (ParseCommand.cs:33; ScriptContext.cs:559-565 does a raw lookup), unlike nearly every other command which substitutes ${var}; a user who writes from: ${cfg} silently hits the empty-source path — warning, empty dictionary, and Ok success (ParseCommand.cs:34-40).
recommendation: Add at least a CiscoIosParser (indentation-scoped blocks: 'interface X' / nested ' description ...' lines — structurally simpler than FortiGate's config/edit/next/end) and a generic template parser (per-line regex with named capture groups, textfsm-style, where the script supplies the patterns) and register them in ParserFactory. In the same pass, make ParseCommand accept ${var} in 'from' by stripping the wrapper before lookup, and fix the doc comment to list the actual formats. The IConfigParser seam already exists, so each new parser is a self-contained class plus one factory line.
user_benefit: A multi-vendor network operator (the explicit audience of this tool) can turn 'show run' output from Cisco/Arista/Juniper into structured variables for foreach/if logic instead of hand-rolling extract regexes per device family. Today parse is useless on anything that isn't FortiOS.

evidence.note: only fortigate/fortios registered; anything else throws
doc claims 'and other formats'; bare-name 'from' lookup with silent-Ok empty-source path
interface doc names 'cisco-ios' as intended format
GetVariableString is a raw variable lookup — '${cfg}' is looked up literally

title: http command cannot download or upload files (string-only body and response)
existing_state: The http command's request body is `StringContent(body, Encoding.UTF8)` from a substituted string (Services/Scripting/Commands/HttpCommand.cs:89, 130-137), and the response is always read with `ReadAsStringAsync` into the `into` variable (HttpCommand.cs:156, 162-169). The allowed-key table (Services/Scripting/ScriptParser.cs:128) has no save-to-file, upload-file, or proxy key. So a script cannot fetch a firmware image, config archive, certificate bundle, or vendor-API binary artifact to disk (the bytes get mangled through string decoding into a variable), nor POST a file as multipart or raw body. The neighboring sftp command covers SSH transfers only — HTTP(S) downloads, which are common in network-device workflows (vendor portals, controller REST APIs), have no path to disk.
recommendation: Add `save_to: <path>` to HttpOptions (Models/ScriptStep.cs http options block): when set, stream `response.Content` to the file (gated through ScriptFileAccessValidator like WriteFileCommand) and capture `into_file`/`into_bytes` instead of decoding the body to a string; skip the response-body debug echo in that mode. Add `body_file: <path>` (raw file body with content_type) and optionally multipart upload. Register the new keys in ScriptParser.cs:128 and the http option parser so validation/autocomplete work, and mirror the fields in the Flow Canvas http block definition per Development Guideline 8.
user_benefit: Closes a real gap for fleet workflows — pull a config backup or OS image from a controller's REST API and push it to devices in one script, instead of shelling out to curl via localcmd (which today also triggers confirmation prompts).

evidence.note: body is substituted string -> StringContent only
response always ReadAsStringAsync into a variable; no file sink
http key whitelist has no save_to/body_file/proxy

title: No strip_ansi() or lines() helpers for cleaning raw SSH output — docs recommend a hand-typed escape-code regex instead
existing_state: There is no built-in to strip ANSI escape sequences from captured output. SCRIPTING.md's own string-function examples tell users to write `- set: clean = regex_replace(output, '/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/', "")` (SCRIPTING.md:1006) — an incantation that only removes SGR color codes and misses cursor-movement CSI sequences, OSC titles, and other escapes that colored/paged device CLIs (modern NX-OS, JunOS, Linux boxes with PROMPT styling) emit. StringFunctions has 16 functions (Services/Scripting/Functions/StringFunctions.cs:30-38 registration tail) with nothing output-oriented; turning _output into iterable lines requires legacy split(output, delimiter) (JsonUtilities.cs:397-416) where the user must guess the right newline delimiter for CRLF-vs-LF transcripts and then compact() the blanks.
recommendation: Add to StringFunctions: strip_ansi(text) using a comprehensive escape regex (CSI, OSC, single-char escapes — well-known pattern, one line with the existing 5s regex timeout convention) and lines(text) that splits on \r\n|\n|\r and optionally drops blank lines (flag arg, default keep). Update the SCRIPTING.md example at line 1006 to use strip_ansi. Both slot into the existing registration block and JsonUtilities.SplitTopLevelCommas plumbing.
user_benefit: Every parse of colored device output starts with de-ANSI-fying and line-splitting; making the first step a memorized regex with a known blind spot is beneath the tool's polish level. One word instead of an escape-code incantation.

evidence.note: Official docs recommend regex_replace(output, '/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/', "") — SGR-only, misses other escape classes
Registration list — no output-cleanup helpers among the 16 string functions
split() with manual delimiter is the only line-splitting path; default delimiter is ','

title: No list aggregation functions: sum/avg/median missing, and min/max cannot take a list
existing_state: MathFunctions registers abs, min, max, round, floor, ceil, random, pow, sqrt, clamp, iif (Services/Scripting/Functions/MathFunctions.cs:14-27) — and that is the entire math surface. min/max iterate scalar varargs only, silently skipping non-numeric args (MathFunctions.cs:37-71), so `min(latencies)` where latencies is a list returns null/garbage rather than the list minimum. There is no sum, avg, median, or mod anywhere (registry, legacy switch, or json.*). The only workaround is reduce() with manual float() casts (CollectionFunctions.cs:58-78 is the one type-preserving collection function), e.g. `reduce(latencies, (acc,x) => acc + float(x), 0)` — and avg additionally needs a separate length() division. Notably the app itself knows users want aggregates: the autocomplete's into-derived suffixes include _avg/_min/_max/_count for the ping command (ScriptAutocompleteProvider.cs:106-114), but script authors processing extracted values get nothing equivalent.
recommendation: In MathFunctions, add sum(list), avg(list), median(list), and mod(a, b); teach min/max to detect a single list-typed argument (resolve via ValueResolver.ResolveListValue, same pattern CollectionFunctions uses) and aggregate over it while keeping the existing varargs behavior. Follow the existing IsInteger int-collapse convention for return values, register the names in MathFunctions.Register, and document in SCRIPTING.md.
user_benefit: Computing 'average latency across 200 devices' or 'total interface errors' is the bread and butter of fleet scripting; today it requires a reduce-lambda-plus-float-cast incantation most users will never find.

evidence.note: Full registration list; min/max are scalar-varargs loops that skip unresolvable args
reduce() is the only aggregation path today; requires a 2-param lambda and manual casts
_avg/_min/_max derived suffixes for ping show the aggregate demand already exists in the product

title: Network function library is thin for a network-device tool: no CIDR math, MAC normalization, or IP arithmetic
existing_state: NetworkFunctions registers exactly five functions: is_valid_ip, ip_version, ip_in_cidr, url_host, url_port (Services/Scripting/Functions/NetworkFunctions.cs:14-21). ip_in_cidr already contains correct v4/v6 prefix-mask logic (lines 36-77), but none of it is exposed for derivation: there is no cidr_network/cidr_broadcast/cidr_netmask/cidr_size, no ip_add/ip_to_int for iterating addresses, no MAC address validation or normalization (Cisco aabb.ccdd.eeff vs IEEE aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff vs dashed — comparing MAC/ARP tables across vendors requires normalizing formats), and no hostname/FQDN validation. For an app whose core use case is running commands against fleets of routers/switches, users currently hand-roll these with regex_replace/split chains.
recommendation: Extend NetworkFunctions (keeping the pure/no-I/O contract stated at line 10): cidr_network(cidr), cidr_broadcast(cidr), cidr_netmask(prefix), cidr_size(cidr) reusing the existing byte/mask code from IpInCidr; ip_add(ip, n) and ip_to_int/int_to_ip via IPAddress byte math; mac_normalize(mac[, format]) accepting colon/dash/dot/bare hex input and emitting a chosen format, plus is_valid_mac(mac); is_valid_hostname(name). Each is a small pure function with the established Resolve/SplitTopLevelCommas plumbing already in the file.
user_benefit: These are the functions a network engineer reaches for daily — compute a gateway from an interface CIDR, normalize a MAC from 'show mac address-table' before comparing against an inventory column, iterate a management subnet. Ansible's ipaddr filter set is the professional benchmark here.

evidence.note: Complete registration list — five functions
v4/v6 prefix masking already implemented inside IpInCidr, ready to factor into derivation helpers

title: No way to open a hosts CSV via command line, file association, or drag-and-drop
existing_state: Program.Main takes no arguments at all (`static void Main()`, Program.cs:13) — `SSH_Helper.exe C:\fleets\core-switches.csv` does nothing with the path, and there is no file-association story. The only drag-and-drop in the app is internal preset/favorites tree reordering (Form1.Designer.cs:566-591; Form1.cs:4620-4662, 5372-5405); the host grid does not accept a dropped .csv from Explorer.
